text:
maria: FYI, the updated package exports in @redwood/sdk@2.1.0 just regressed our onboarding sample on node/cjs consumers. stack traces in CI.

kevin: ugh, what exactly changed?

maria: We moved to an exports map to be explicit for edge/runtime, e.g. in package.json:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
That makes Node require() pick up the ESM entry and then apps using `require('@redwood/sdk')` explode with: `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module`.

zach: Oof. Edge runtimes like Vercel and Bun are fine with the mjs entry, but lots of existing sample apps (and internal infra) still use CJS.

priya: Is this just require() consumers, or do types break too?

maria: Both. Our `types` field was left pointing at `dist/esm/index.d.ts` which doesn't match some bundlers' resolution. TS projects that `import sdk = require('@redwood/sdk')` fail type resolution.

kevin: Short-term workaround: publish a dual entry using conditional exports, e.g.
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
},
"main": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs",
"module": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
"types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
```
That keeps CJS consumers working and gives edge runtimes the right file.

dev-bot: CI job #4456: onboarding-samples/runner failed on node 16 in sample-app-2 (exit code 1)

zach: Can we also add a tiny compatibility note in the SDK changelog + an automated smoke test in CI that runs the sample app in both `require` and `import` modes?

priya: Agreed. Also need to ensure our rollup/tsc outputs both cjs and esm artifacts AND emit a single `.d.ts` set that maps correctly. Some bundlers expect types next to CJS entry.

maria: I'll open an issue with action items: publish patch with conditional exports + main/module/types + add sample-app smoke test + update changelog. tagging @eng-devex for visibility.

kevin: If we want a hotfix, revert the exports change and release 2.1.1 to unblock onboarding. Then do the dual-entry in 2.1.2 with tests.

maria: good plan. I'll also add a note about auth parity: one of the failing samples used our browser auth shim that assumes `fetch` present; node-cjs consumers didn't pick up the runtime wrapper. We should validate auth/retry behavior across runtimes in the smoke test too.

zach: thanks — let's avoid surprise breakages like this. :pray:
